notes.raw:
Heat capacity (cal/mol·K) and enthalpy (kcal/mol) equations: 
298.15-3000 K: $Cp^{0} = 8.067 + 0.470 \times 10^{-3} T - 0.541 \times 10^{5} T^{-2}$ 
$H^{0}-H_{298}^{0}=8.067\times10^{-3}T+0.235\times10^{-6}T^{2}+0.541\times10^{2}T^{-1}-2.608$ 
Reaction equations (kcal/mol): 
298.15-2000 K: $\Delta \mathrm{Hr}^{\circ} = 47.694 + 0.637 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{T} - 0.220 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{T}^{2} + 23.900 \mathrm{T}^{-1}$ 
$\Delta \mathrm{Gr}^{\circ} = 47.694 - 0.637 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{T} \ln \mathrm{T} + 0.220 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{T}^{2} + 11.950 \mathrm{T}^{-1} + 1.351 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{T}$ 
2000-3000 K: $\Delta Hr^{\circ} = 50.056 - 1.010 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{T} + 0.157 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{T}^{2} - 1121.900 \mathrm{T}^{-1}$ 
$\Delta \mathrm{Gr}^{\circ} = 50.056 + 1.010 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{T} \ln \mathrm{T} - 0.157 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{T}^{2} - 560.950 \mathrm{T}^{-1} - 11.456 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{T}$ 
Sources: Enthalpy of formation at 298 K based on O'Hare (87), Gaydon (43), and Somayajulu (109). Other data based on Herzberg (52).
